title: Fixed-source cylinder prism in a relative join
statement:
Use simplicial sets, products, degreewise pushouts, standard simplices and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and relative joins with their structure maps and canonical inclusions of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. Let $Z,X$ be simplicial sets in a fixed universe and let $x:\Delta^0\to X$ be a vertex. Put $C_Z=\Delta^0\amalg_{Z\times\{0\}}(Z\times\Delta^1)$, where the first map collapses $Z\times\{0\}$ to the point $p$. Denote the quotient map by $c:Z\times\Delta^1\to C_Z$ and its top endpoint by $c_1:Z\to C_Z$. Put $K=(Z\times X)\amalg_{Z}C_Z$, gluing $z\mapsto(z,x)$ to $c_1$. Write $j:Z\times X\to K$ and $k:C_Z\to K$ for its maps. Let $a:K\to X$ restrict to the projection on $Z\times X$ and the constant map at $x$ on $C_Z$. Put $T=K\star_X X$ for $a$ and $1_X$, with inclusions $i_K,i_X$ and structure map $\pi:T\to X$, and write $v$ for the apex of $Z^{\triangleright}$.

There exist simplicial maps $P:Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T$ over $X$ and $J:Z^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to T$ over the constant vertex $x$, with the following exact restrictions:
$$P|_{Z\times X}=i_Kj,\qquad P|_{\{v\}\times X}=i_X,$$
$$J|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{0\}}=i_K k(p),\qquad J|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{1\}}=P|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{x\}},\qquad J|_{Z\times\Delta^1}=i_Kkc.$$
Moreover $J|_{\{v\}\times\Delta^1}$ is the relative-join edge from $k(p)$ in the initial $K$ to $x$ in the final $X$, with its degeneracies. The same conclusions hold when $Z$ is empty. No quasicategory, fibration, filteredness or colimit hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For an $n$-simplex of $Z^{\triangleright}\times X$, write the cone factor $u\in(Z\star\Delta^0)_n$ in its join block form of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] as $(\delta,z)$, where $\delta:[n]\to[1]$ is monotone, $z$ is the simplex of $Z$ on the initial block $I=\delta^{-1}(0)$ (and $I$ may be empty), and write $\sigma\in X_n$ for the second factor. Define $\epsilon=\delta$ and a simplex of $K\star X$ with initial block $I$ labelled by $j(z,\sigma|_I)$ and final block labelled by $\sigma|_{\delta^{-1}(1)}$; when a block is empty use the formal degree $-1$ element. The compatibility equation for the relative join holds because $a j(z,\sigma|_I)=\sigma|_I$ and the second factor maps by $1_X$. The resulting pair $(w,(\epsilon,\sigma))$ is therefore an $n$-simplex of $T=K\star_X X$. As $\delta$, restrictions of $z$, and restrictions of $\sigma$ all commute with a simplicial operator, these assignments define a simplicial map $P:Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T$, and its structure map is the projection to $\sigma$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, second specialization on printed p. 433; explicit degreewise simplicial construction

proof.text: For an $n$-simplex $(u,t)$ of $Z^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1$, use the same block form $(\delta,z)$ for $u$, with $I=\delta^{-1}(0)$, and put $\epsilon=\delta\wedge t$, the pointwise minimum of the two monotone maps to $[1]$. Its zero block is $E_0=I\cup I'$, where the tail $I'=\delta^{-1}(1)\cap t^{-1}(0)$ follows $I$. If $I'\neq\varnothing$, monotonicity of $t$ forces $t=0$ on all of $E_0$; then label the $K$-factor of $E_0$ by the degenerate simplex $k(p)$ of dimension $|E_0|-1$ (this includes $I=\varnothing$ and $Z=\varnothing$). If $I'=\varnothing$, then $E_0=I$ and label it by $kc(z,t|_I)$, the formal degree $-1$ element when $I=\varnothing$. The two rules agree when both apply ($I'=\varnothing$, $t|_I=0$), since $c(z,0)=p$ by the quotient relation. On the one block $\epsilon^{-1}(1)$ label the $X$-factor by the constant simplex at $x$. Since $ak$ is constant at $x$, $(a\star1_X)$ of this join simplex equals $\rho_X(\epsilon,x_n)$, so $(w,(\epsilon,x_n))$ is an $n$-simplex of $T$. For monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $(\delta\wedge t)\alpha=\delta\alpha\wedge t\alpha$, the blocks pull back to $\alpha^{-1}(I)$ and $\alpha^{-1}(I')$, the condition $t=0$ on $E_0$ is preserved, $\alpha^*k(p)$ is degenerate at $k(p)$ and $\alpha^*kc(z,t|_I)=kc(\alpha^*z,t\alpha|)$; when a tail first appears after restriction the agreement of the two rules applies. Hence these assignments commute with the operators of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] and define $J:Z^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to T$ with $\pi J$ the constant vertex $x$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, second specialization on printed p. 433; explicit degreewise simplicial construction

proof.text: If $t=0$, then $\epsilon=0$ and every $Z$ value is sent through $c(-,0)=p$, so the whole simplex is the pure $K$-simplex $i_Kk(p)$; hence $J|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{0\}}=i_Kk(p)$. If $t=1$, then $\epsilon=\delta$, there is no tail, the $Z$ block is labelled $kc_1(z)=j(z,x|_I)$ by the gluing of $K$, and the final block is sent to the constant $x$, which is exactly the formula for $P(-,x)$; hence $J|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{1\}}=P|_{Z^{\triangleright}\times\{x\}}$. On the pure $Z$ subobject one has $\delta=0$, so the formula is the pure $K$-simplex $i_Kkc$, giving $J|_{Z\times\Delta^1}=i_Kkc$. For the pure apex of $Z^{\triangleright}$, $\delta=1$: the formula has the $k(p)$ endpoint at $t=0$ and the $x$ endpoint at $t=1$, with the relative-join degeneracies, so it is the required edge from $k(p)$ to $x$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, second specialization on printed p. 433; explicit degreewise simplicial construction

proof.text: When $Z=\varnothing$, the initial blocks are always empty, $C_Z=K=\Delta^0$ and $a$ is the constant map at $x$. The preceding formulas reduce to $P=i_X$ and to the relative-join edge from the unique $K$ vertex to $x$, so all four restrictions and the apex assertion remain valid. Thus the maps exist for arbitrary $Z$ and $X$ with no quasicategory, fibration, filteredness, or colimit assumptions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q138-7d3debe41 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, its four steps, the three cited definitions in full, and step 8 of lem-coef-filtered-cocartesian-section-cofinality, which cites the item. The construction is correct and each step is elementary. Step 1 defines P with epsilon = delta and labels j(z, sigma|_I) and sigma|_{I^c}; it restricts to i_K j and i_X. Step 2 defines J with epsilon = delta wedge t, using that a k is constant at x. Step 3 checks the four exact restrictions and the apex edge. Step 4 covers Z empty, where C_Z = K = Z^triangleright = Delta^0. I tested Z = Delta^0 with X = Delta^0 or Delta^1, plus Z empty. I made three fixes in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-relative-join-fixed-source-prism.json. (1) C3/B3: the steps use the join block form of Z^triangleright and K star X, which is defined in def-coef-infinity-relative-cone, but did not cite it; I added it to the uses of steps 1-4 and to proof_deps. (2) E5: as written, step 2 gave the empty label when I is empty, which is wrong when I is empty and the tail is nonempty (the apex at t = 0, or Z empty). That zero block must carry the degenerate k(p). The step also never stated that a nonempty tail forces t = 0 on I, and it asserted rather than checked that the construction respects the simplicial operators. I rewrote step 2 as an explicit two-case rule; the two cases agree because c(z,0) = p, and the operator check is now written out. (3) Step 3 now states the gluing identity k c_1(z) = j(z,x). The statement is unchanged, there are no new nodes, and there are no tool_uses.
